clue.text: Champion more coarse about South American

indicators.note: the comparative adjective goes around the two abbreviations, enclosing them

parts.note: cruder means more coarse or vulgar
S is the compass abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: A sports champion is described as rougher than some South American rival.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader campaigns zealously for a cause, so a champion of it fits as a synonym.

parts.note: a snap is a sharp crack, as of a twig breaking
a good shot is a skilled marksman

explanation.surface: A crack marksman, one of the best, is asked whether they are still active.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' reads as an adjective (expert) qualifying 'marksman', but it is a noun giving its own piece; 'still' is a noun, a single photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single photographic frame, and a quick casual photograph is exactly that; the question mark flags the noun sense.

indicators.note: in a down entry the stand piece is placed beneath the abbreviation for with

parts.note: an easel is a stand for a painter's canvas

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stand below alongside a crafty person.
explanation.definitionFit: A slyboots is a cunning, sneaky person, and calling someone a weasel means the same in informal speech.

parts.note: Aries, the ram, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone shows dissent by flicking a rude V-sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'V-sign' looks like the rude gesture but splits into the letter V and a star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To vary is to differ, and accounts or figures that differ can be said to disagree.

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
a nun is a religious sister
to court someone is to date them

explanation.surface: A tennis-playing sister dominates her opponent on court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' sounds like a tennis court but is the verb meaning to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to flood, so figuratively to swamp or overwhelm with too much.

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
a range is an assortment or selection of goods

explanation.surface: Someone declares their love for a selection of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange is a common citrus fruit, an example of the category.

definitions.meaning: a love affair or passionate attachment
as a verb, to exaggerate or invent fanciful stories

explanation.surface: Someone loves telling tall tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair is called this, and as a verb it means to embellish facts with fanciful invention.

clue.text: What movement of timer could be worth

indicators.note: a movement shifts things around, so the letters of the clock word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what a moving clock mechanism might be worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' suggests a clock's works, which suits 'timer', but here it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is value or excellence deserving reward, a close synonym of worth.

parts.note: a train of events is a series of them

explanation.surface: A tutor appears in the hospital television drama ER.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ER' looks like the name of the TV series, but it is just two letters added to a synonym of series.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer coaches or instructs people, as a tutor does.

clue.text: Loud noise made by half of them below

indicators.note: only the opening two of the four letters of the word them are kept

parts.note: under means below or beneath

explanation.surface: A loud noise is made by half the people downstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunder is the loud rumbling following lightning, and figuratively any booming sound.

parts.note: to trip is to slip or stumble

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take off a second underskirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' looks like the undergarment, which suits 'Remove', but it is the verb meaning to stumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to take off or take away, as in stripping paint or clothes.

clue.text: Fungal problem — mate is scheduled for treatment

indicators.note: treatment works material over and changes it, so these letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: A friend is booked in for treatment of a fungal infection.
explanation.definitionFit: This tree blight is caused by a fungus spread by bark beetles, so it is a fungal problem.

indicators.note: a condemned building is torn down and rebuilt, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A newspaper article criticised a poetry reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a public performance, such as one of poems read aloud to an audience.

clue.text: A red wine in tavern and cousin began raving

indicators.note: something raving is wild or deranged, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: In a pub, a relative started ranting about red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: This well-known blend name denotes a popular red grape variety and the red wine made from it.

clue.text: With great enthusiasm, similar to mother and daughter

parts.note: like means similar to
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: An eager daughter is just like her mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very energetically or intensely, i.e. with great enthusiasm.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
dress is formal or ceremonial attire, as in full dress

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a matter of formal attire.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to remedy or correct it, i.e. put it right.

clue.text: Make little of sad theatrical production

parts.note: feeling down means feeling sad
a play is a theatrical production

explanation.surface: Someone belittles a gloomy stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: To make little of something is to minimise its importance, which is to understate it.

parts.note: sees means recognises or perceives
tars is an old word for sailors

explanation.surface: Someone notices that sailors are feeling woozy.
explanation.definitionFit: After a blow to the head one is said to glimpse flashes of light in the sky, i.e. to feel dazed.

clue.text: Written down at home by opponents playing chess?

parts.note: in means at home
the two sides in chess are named after their colours, the dark and light pieces

explanation.surface: A chess game between rivals at home is recorded on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means set down in writing or print, dark ink on light paper.

clue.text: Charge made by international male model

parts.note: to model is to pose for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: A fee is charged by a male model working worldwide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like a noun (a fee) but is the verb, to levy.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose a tax or fine is to levy or charge it on someone.

clue.text: Artist wearing an acceptable type of jacket

indicators.note: the acceptable word has the artist inside it, as clothing holds its wearer

parts.note: OK means acceptable
RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: A painter dons a passable jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is a hooded waterproof jacket, one particular kind of jacket.

parts.note: Norma is an opera by Vincenzo Bellini
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A music student is studying a characteristic Bellini work.
explanation.walkthrough: L is a learner because British learner drivers display an L-plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal means usual or standard, so typical is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Marauder blowing top, up in arms

indicators.note: losing one's top means the opening letter of the raider word is dropped

parts.note: a pirate is a marauder at sea

explanation.surface: A raider loses their temper and gets furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blowing top' reads as losing one's temper, which suits the definition, but it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Up in arms is an idiom for angry and protesting, so furious or angry is the sense.

indicators.note: being called back makes the agent word run in the opposite direction

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, acts as an agent
former means bygone or of an earlier time

explanation.surface: An agent remembered an entertainer from times past.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer, such as a singer or dancer who appears on stage.

parts.note: a plan is an idea or scheme

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word that is kept

explanation.surface: Someone praises an idea that works from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a verb but is the noun: a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is an industrial installation, the same as works meaning a factory.

clue.text: Race official saw red, mad about leader in Toyota

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the single letter, enclosing it
something mad is crazy and out of order, so these letters are jumbled
the first letter of the car brand is taken

explanation.surface: A race official got angry and furious with a Toyota driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw red, mad' shuffles to SEWARD, and 'about' puts it around T.
explanation.definitionFit: At a horse or motor race, an official overseeing the rules is called a steward.

clue.text: A dabbler, friend invested in gold and silver, ultimately

indicators.note: the friend word is put inside the gold symbol, as money is put into something

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
mate is an informal word for friend

indicators.note: only the final letter of silver is used

explanation.surface: A dilettante friend has put money into gold and silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' looks financial, suiting gold and silver, but it is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur does something without professional skill, so a dabbler, someone who tries a thing casually, fits.
